units: INR crore unless stated. Company PPTs/ARs report in INR crore (no conversion). Broker figures quoted in INR mn (PL, MOSL) have been converted to crore where noted (1 crore = 10 mn). Segment EBIT = company "segment results / operational EBIT" (profit before interest, tax and unallocable items). companyEbitda = company-defined EBIDTA (includes other income, before exchange-fluctuation (ECF) loss). Segment EBITDA = segment EBIT + segment D&A (derived). Capital employed = segment assets - segment liabilities (derived, closing).

growth.comment: Derived from AR product revenue; Axis Capital also cites specialty ~-6% and refrigerant gas ~+60% in FY26.

Fluoro: higher volumes across refrigerants, industrial chemicals and fluoropolymers plus better realisations offset raw-material inflation. Specialty: "steady performance despite challenging market"; early signs of agro volume and price recovery in core products.

Chemicals +25% YoY driven by fluorochemicals (higher HFC volumes and realisations, new markets offsetting softer US). Specialty subdued: China overcapacity, pricing pressure; chemicals EBIT margin 25.4% vs 28.9% YoY, entire decline attributed to specialty by Kotak.

chemSplit.specialtyPipeline: 7-8 agro products in very advanced state with customers (May-2026); 6-7 AIs in kitty, earlier talk of US$400-500mn peak revenue (analyst question, Jul-2026) - timing depends on innovator registrations; registrations for two AIs progressing in Brazil (Oct-2026); two Western pharma innovators, one oncology molecule to contribute "very quickly".

srfPosition.fact: HFC capacity to exceed 65,000 tpa after Rs88cr debottlenecking (approved May-2026); plants run at maximum capacity to maximise quota baseline (CY2024-26).
Analyst estimate of SRF R32 capacity ~27,000-28,000 t; management declined to confirm capacity numbers. India domestic R32 demand ~17,000-18,000 t (CMD, Jan-2026).
FY26 refrigerant/fluoro product revenue Rs3,598cr vs Rs2,250cr in FY25 (+60%): "record year in terms of both realizations and volumes".

Anti-dumping duty on R32 imports from China in force ~3 years; sunset review due Dec-2026; CMD says hard to justify as prices are healthy and India pricing independent of ADD. India imposed ADD on R-134a (~Jan-2026) which does not bind as global prices are above the threshold.

US: R32 subject to US tariffs - contracts moved from long-term to consignment-by-consignment; US demand softer (destocking, low-GWP transition); volumes redirected to Middle East and new markets. Middle East shipments disrupted for ~half of Q4FY26 by the regional conflict, recovered in Q1FY27 ("Floron commands differentiated pricing").
Management view: refrigerant demand and pricing to remain broadly stable barring seasonality (Oct-2026); Q2/Q3 weaker than Q1 seasonally.

quotaRegimes.fact: 2026 national HFC production quota 797,800 t; Juhua 299,900 t (37.58%); top six firms ~90% of quota; draft 2027 quota largely keeps 2026 framework; controlled use to fall to 90% of baseline by 1-Jan-2029.

Baseline = average HFC production/consumption of CY2024-26 plus 65% of HCFC-22 2009-10 baseline; freeze from 1-Jan-2028; cuts of 10% by 2032, 20% by 2037, 30% by 2042, 85% by 2047. SRF: CY2027 is a "free year" (anyone with capacity may sell); quotas from 1-Jan-2028 go to 2024-26 producers; MoEFCC 1-Apr-2026 circular requires new capacity to be up by 31-Dec-2027. Government retains right to include HCFC; final view likely early 2027.
quotaRegimes.confidence: Kigali schedule from search-result extract of MoEFCC document; SRF statements from transcripts.

quotaRegimes.fact: HFC allowance cap 60% of baseline 2024-28, 30% 2029-33, 20% 2034-35, 15% from 2036.
Provisional agreement: complete phase-out of HFC consumption by 2050; production phased down to 15% by 2036.

hfo.fact: Odisha (Gopalpur, ~300-acre site) next-gen refrigerant project: ~Rs2,300cr over 2 years (revised May-2026 from Oct-2024 approval) for 20,000 tpa HFO (1234yf, 1234ze, 1233zd) + 30,000 tpa HF + electronic-grade HF; in-house non-infringing process; environmental clearance received; commissioning Feb-2028 / Q4FY28; meaningful volumes 8-12 months after; management expects to be top 3-4 refrigerant makers globally; HFO pricing "significantly north of typical HFC pricing" even post-patent expiry.

drivers: Chemicals Rs2,315cr (+26%), EBIT margin 27.6%: refrigerant volumes and realisations strong (harsh global summer), HFC plants at high utilisation, Middle East recovered; raw-material inflation from supply-chain disruption passed through.

Performance Films & Foil Rs2,017cr (+42%), EBIT 17.3% vs 9.9%: Middle East war shut competitor capacity; SRF ran flat out with global/DTA sourcing; customer panic buying lifted prices; low-cost inventory gains. CFO: "In a perverse way, the war has helped us".
Technical Textiles EBIT 18.1% vs 8.1%: demand recovery plus inventory gains; belting exports to US after tariff rationalisation; PIY helped by QCO stay order from May-2026.
Below the line: ECF (forex) loss Rs102cr on long-dated export hedges after sharp rupee depreciation.

q2fy27.vsExpectations: EBITDA missed: PL est Rs1,002cr; MOSL est Rs1,070cr (margin est 23.2%); Kotak: EBITDA 2.6% below its estimate and 8.4% below consensus; Mint: 9% below consensus. Revenue beat (MOSL est Rs4,600cr).
drivers: Chemicals Rs2,079cr (+25% YoY, -10% QoQ), EBIT Rs528cr (+10%), margin 25.4% vs 28.9%: higher HFC volumes and realisations, new markets (Middle East) offsetting softer US; PTFE mix shifting to value-added grades. Margin hit by raw-material, freight (15-20%+ on some routes) and fuel inflation; specialty under China overcapacity pricing pressure (Kotak: entire margin decline from specialty).

Performance Films & Foil Rs2,122cr (+51%), EBIT Rs206cr (+73%), margin 9.7% (17.3% in Q1): record packed production; demand moderated after Q1 inventory build; Q1 low-cost inventory benefit absent; foil exports to Europe strong, Tetra Pak-type aseptic qualification.
Technical Textiles Rs595cr (+25%), EBIT Rs72cr (+71%), 12.2% margin: record belting fabrics exports, N66/PTCF scale-up; no one-offs.
Forex: further ECF loss ~Rs63cr. Working capital lengthened with crude price jump (Kotak). Gross debt ~Rs5,200cr vs ~Rs5,000cr at Mar-26; CFO Rs790cr H1 (MOSL).
New capex: Rs600cr battery-grade aluminium foil plant.
callCommentary: Chemicals growth guidance 15-20% reiterated, towards higher end for FY27.
Refrigerant pricing/demand expected broadly stable; plants to run full through Dec-31-2026 baseline end; declined to disclose capacity.
Agro: registrations for two AIs progressing (e.g. Brazil); H2 volume-led ramp. Pharma: two meaningful Western innovators, one oncology molecule to start contributing soon.
HFO on track for Q4FY28; Chemours FEP/FKM first plant Q4FY27, second Q1FY28; PVDF capitalisation on track; semiconductor chemicals still in lab optimisation.
Foil business profitable by year-end; battery foil needs ~2 years qualification; declined to guide 15% margin (PL notes margins expected ~15%).
Some freight cost increases cannot be passed through in price-sensitive markets.

All PPE capitalised through CWIP; CWIP Rs1,889cr at Mar-26 (Rs811cr Mar-25); >Rs680cr capitalised in FY26. New plants take a couple of quarters to ramp after capitalisation - depreciation precedes revenue.
Q1FY27 films and textiles margins included low-cost inventory gains that reversed in Q2FY27.

Chemours plants on return-on-investment style arrangement; refrigerant pricing import-parity based.
